summary.text: Glenn Thompson is the Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 15th District and won re-election on November 3, 2026.

A Howard, Pennsylvania, native, he spent 28 years as a therapist, rehabilitation services manager and licensed nursing home administrator before his election to Congress in 2008. He has served since 2009 (the old 5th District through 2018) and chairs the House Committee on Agriculture.

paragraphs.text: Thompson was born in Howard, Pennsylvania, in 1959, and his House website calls him a life-long resident of Howard.
He earned a bachelor's degree in therapeutic rehabilitation from Pennsylvania State University in 1981 and a Master of Education from Temple University in 1998.

Before his election to Congress he spent 28 years as a therapist, rehabilitation services manager and licensed nursing home administrator, and he has served as a volunteer firefighter for more than three decades, according to his House website.

Thompson was a member of the Bald Eagle Area School Board from 1990 to 1996, and his House website also lists service as past vice-chair of the Private Industry Council of the Central Corridor and as a Workforce Investment Board member.

An Eagle Scout, he has volunteered for more than 30 years with the Juniata Valley Boy Scout Council as Scoutmaster, executive board member and Council President, and he received the National Distinguished Eagle Scout Award in 2012.

Thompson won the November 4, 2008 general election for Pennsylvania's 5th District, defeating Democrat Mark McCracken and Libertarian James Fryman, and took office in 2009; he has represented the 15th District since boundaries were redrawn in 2019.
He was appointed to the House Committee on Education & Workforce in 2009 and now serves as a senior member, and he chairs the House Committee on Agriculture, per his House website.

He has been Co-Chairman of the bipartisan Congressional Career and Technical Education Caucus for more than a decade, and his House website says his Career and Technical Education for the 21st Century Act, introduced in the 115th Congress, passed the House and Senate unanimously and was signed into law.
According to his House website, Thompson and his wife, Penny Ammerman-Thompson, have three adult sons and two grandsons, and live in Howard.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 63.8% of the vote to Ray Bilger's 36.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
